excerpts.text: Each dimension shall have a tolerance. Dimensions shall not be duplicated or the same information given in two different ways; double dimensioning can lead to conflicting requirements after a change.
A feature control frame that references a datum requires a corresponding datum feature symbol on the drawing. A referenced datum that is not defined makes the tolerance unverifiable.
Reference dimensions are enclosed in parentheses and are not toleranced; they are for information only and are not used for inspection.

A position tolerance controls the location of a feature of size relative to datums. The tolerance zone is a cylinder when the diameter symbol precedes the tolerance value. MMC allows a bonus tolerance as the feature departs from maximum material condition.
Circular and total runout are referenced to a datum axis, typically established by two datum features (A-B) or a single cylindrical datum feature.
Chain dimensioning accumulates tolerance. The overall dimension of a chained set should be shown as reference or basic, or one link left undimensioned, to avoid over-constraint.
The drawing shall state the linear units used. Where both SI and U.S. customary values appear, the primary units are stated and the alternate units are shown in brackets.
The title block identifies the drawing number, revision, title, material, finish, approvals and sheet count. Approval fields are complete before release.
For metric threads the tap drill diameter is approximately the major diameter minus the pitch (M6x1.0 tap drill 5.0). A hole at or above the major diameter cannot be tapped; it is a clearance hole.
Every item on a parts list is identified on the drawing with a find number balloon, and every balloon corresponds to a parts list entry. Quantities on the parts list agree with the assembly.
